cards.explanation: The scattering falls on every one of them alike. Isaiah lists people and priest alike, servant and master, maid and mistress, buyer and seller, lender and borrower, creditor and debtor (Isaiah 24:2). It's a long list, friends, and nobody gets skipped. Nobody gets a special lane.

The answer is False. Isaiah never calls it his own guess. He says, "For the LORD has spoken this word." (Isaiah 24:3) The weight of it rests on who spoke, friends, and the prophet is just passing it along.

The answer is the everlasting covenant. Isaiah says, "they have transgressed the laws; they have overstepped the decrees and broken the everlasting covenant." (Isaiah 24:5) Three things are named there, and the covenant is the third. It's a heavy list, friends, so let's keep tracking it together.
The answer is False. Isaiah says, "…and only a few survive." (Isaiah 24:6) That means not everyone does. This is one of the heavy verses, friends, so we'll take it slow and keep going.

The answer is that they all groan. Isaiah says, "All the merrymakers now groan." (Isaiah 24:7) The new wine dried up and the vine withered, and the party people go from cheering to groaning. That's quite a change in mood, bakers.

The word is bitter. Isaiah says, "strong drink is bitter to those who consume it." (Isaiah 24:9) That's the word that fits the blank, friends. The verse also says the people no longer sing and drink wine.
The word is gloom. Isaiah says, "All joy turns to gloom; rejoicing is exiled from the land." (Isaiah 24:11) Rejoicing is pushed right out of the land, friends. Gloom takes its seat.
The answer is True. Isaiah says, "The city is left in ruins; its gate is reduced to rubble." (Isaiah 24:12) The city is in ruins and its gate is rubble. Easy one, bakers, but a good one to hold onto.

The two pictures are a harvested olive tree and leftover grapes. Isaiah says it will be "…like a harvested olive tree, like a gleaning after a grape harvest." (Isaiah 24:13) Both pictures show what's left after the picking is done, friends. I think that's a powerful way to say how little is left.

The song is "Glory to the Righteous One." Isaiah says, "From the ends of the earth we hear singing: “Glory to the Righteous One.”…" (Isaiah 24:16) After all that ruin, friends, a song rises from the farthest places. Now THAT is a sound worth hearing.

The prophet reacts with woe for himself. He says, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me." (Isaiah 24:16) Singing is heard from the ends of the earth, and he answers with a woe. I think he says it twice because he means it, friends.

The answer is no, because escaping one leads into the next. Isaiah says, "Whoever flees the sound of panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare." (Isaiah 24:18) Fleeing the panic lands in the pit, and climbing out of the pit lands in the snare, bakers. The verse before it says terror, pit and snare await the "…dweller of the earth." (Isaiah 24:17)

The earth staggers like a drunkard. Isaiah says, "The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack." (Isaiah 24:20) The ground itself can't stand up straight, friends. That's a picture you won't forget.

The word is rebellion. Isaiah says, "Earth’s rebellion weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again." (Isaiah 24:20) Rebellion is the weight on the earth in this verse, friends. A heavy word for a heavy verse.

The blanks are heaven and earth. Isaiah says, "In that day the LORD will punish the host of heaven above and the kings of the earth below." (Isaiah 24:21) The LORD's reach goes up above, friends, not just down here. And the kings of the earth below don't stand above it all either, because His reach goes down to them too.

The reason is that the LORD of Hosts will reign. Isaiah says, "The moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed; for the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem…" (Isaiah 24:23) The verse gives it right after the "for," friends. That's where the whole message lands.

The answer is False. Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will reign "…before His elders with great glory." (Isaiah 24:23) His elders are there to see it, friends, and the word is glory. Nothing about it is hidden.
